title: Mara and the Portrait
premise: Insurance investigator Vesper Voss receives two letters about the same death: one from a stranger confessing to the drowning of shipping magnate Alden Marsh, the other promising that the real killer will strike again unless Voss delivers a hidden portrait. The portrait, painted by Marsh's daughter-in-law, supposedly shows the face of a witness everyone believes drowned with him — a maid named Mara. As Voss follows the tide of evidence from the Marsh estate's drowned wing to a decommissioned lighthouse, he discovers Mara alive, hidden by those who used her testimony to steal an inheritance. In the end, Voss must choose between handing the portrait to the courts — where the Marsh heirs' money will bury the truth — or letting Mara's own justice, delivered outside the law, stand.
about_author: Edmund Vane is the pen name of a former marine surveyor who spent eleven years investigating coastal losses for Lloyd's syndicates before turning to fiction. He writes in a converted net loft on the Cornish coast, where the tide still dictates his working hours.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Vesper Voss, an insurance investigator with a photographic memory, opens two letters postmarked the same day: a full confession to Alden Marsh's drowning, and a second letter warning that the confessor is lying and that more deaths will follow. Voss recognizes identical pen pressure in both. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: cold curiosity sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: The Drowned Wing
chapters.summary: Voss travels to Blackwater House, the Marsh estate, and tours the flooded west wing where Alden Marsh supposedly fell into the sea during a storm. The widow, Cressida Marsh, performs grief beautifully, but Voss's memory flags a detail: the tide chart on the wall contradicts the official time of death. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: the first crack in an airtight story.

chapters.title: A Maid Called Mara
chapters.summary: Interviewing staff, Voss learns of Mara Quill, a maid who allegedly drowned the same night and whose death closed the inquest. No one will say what she witnessed. A gardener lets slip that Mara's body was never found. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: the sense that a person has been erased on purpose.

chapters.title: The Confessor
chapters.summary: Voss traces the confession's author to a retired harbormaster, Josiah Pell, who repeats his confession word for word — too word for word, as if rehearsed. When Voss quotes a discrepancy back at him, Pell's composure breaks: he was paid to confess, and the payer's name terrifies him. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: pity curdling into alarm.

chapters.title: Portrait of a Missing Face
chapters.summary: Cressida shows Voss the estate's art, including a seascape by her late daughter-in-law, Evie Marsh — but one canvas is missing from the ledger. The second letter demanded 'the portrait.' Voss realizes the painting shows the night of the drowning, and a face on it that shouldn't exist. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: the case turns from fraud to conspiracy.

chapters.title: Evie's Studio
chapters.summary: Voss breaks into the sealed studio of Evie Marsh, the daughter-in-law who left the estate after the drowning. Under fresh varnish he finds an underpainting: Alden Marsh alive at the water's edge, and a small figure watching — a woman in a maid's apron. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: the thrill of holding proof no one wants found.

chapters.title: The Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: Alden's son, Tobias Marsh, confronts Voss with lawyers and a generous retainer to close the file. Tobias is brittle, drinking, and terrified — not of exposure, Voss notes, but of someone specific. A threat arrives that night at Voss's inn. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: pressure applied, and the wrong kind of fear identified.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: The harbormaster Pell is found drowned — the second letter's promise, kept. Voss searches Pell's boathouse and finds a ledger of payments signed with a solicitor's mark: Halloran, the Marsh family's man of business. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: grief for a man used as a decoy, and resolve hardening.

chapters.title: The Solicitor's Silence
chapters.summary: Voss corners solicitor Ambrose Halloran, who invokes privilege until Voss recites the payment ledger from memory. Halloran admits handling money but insists he was protecting the family from 'the true instrument' — and that the portrait must never reach an inquest. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: the law revealed as a lock, not a shield.

chapters.title: Letter Three
chapters.summary: A third letter reaches Voss, this one in a different hand: Mara's own, or someone claiming to be her. It names the lighthouse at Gannet Point and a time — the spring tide. Cressida, watching Voss read it, goes white. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: the hunt inverting — now he is being summoned.

chapters.title: Cressida's Version
chapters.summary: Cressida finally talks: Alden was cruel, the marriage a contract, and on the storm night she saw him alive after the supposed death — with Mara. She believes Mara killed him and has been hiding since. Her testimony is convincing and possibly rehearsed; Voss's memory catches a reused phrase from her first interview. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: sympathy weaponized, and detected.

chapters.title: The Daughter-in-Law
chapters.summary: Voss finds Evie Marsh living under another name in a fishing village. She confesses she painted the portrait from what she saw that night, then hid it when Tobias threatened to destroy it — and her. She gives Voss its hiding place but begs him not to find the woman in it. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: an ally gained, and a warning weighed.

chapters.title: Gannet Point
chapters.summary: Voss reaches the lighthouse at low tide and finds signs of long habitation: tinned food, a woman's boots, tide tables marked for months. Someone has been waiting here, watching the sea — and watching for him. A figure watches from the gallery and vanishes. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: awe and the vertigo of a ghost made flesh.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Mara Quill comes to Voss on her own terms. She saw Alden Marsh die — not by her hand, but by Tobias's, during a violent confrontation over the will. She fled; the family declared her dead and bought a confession to bury the truth. POV: Mara, her first. Emotional beat: a witness reclaiming her own name.

chapters.title: The Inheritance
chapters.summary: Mara reveals the motive: Alden was changing his will that week, cutting Tobias out in favor of a trust administered through — of all people — Halloran, with Mara as a named witness to the signature. Her testimony is worth everything, which is why everyone swears she is dead. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: understanding the machinery that ground her down.

chapters.title: Retainer Revoked
chapters.summary: The Marsh lawyers move: Voss is dismissed, his inn room searched, Evie's village visited by men asking about a painter. The second letter's author reveals themselves in a final note — Halloran, confessing he arranged deaths to protect the estate's version of events. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: isolation, and the choice sharpening.

chapters.title: The Portrait Surfaces
chapters.summary: Voss retrieves the portrait from its hiding place beneath Evie's old studio floor. Tobias's men intercept him on the causeway; in the struggle the canvas is slashed — but Voss has already committed every inch of it to memory, photographically. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: loss converted into an unstealable advantage.

chapters.title: The Inquest Reopened
chapters.summary: Voss forces the issue by petitioning the coroner with the payment ledger, Pell's boathouse evidence, and his sworn recitation of the underpainting. The inquest reopens; Tobias's counsel moves to discredit a dead maid's testimony. Cressida, cornered, hesitates on the stand. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: justice entering the machine that was built to stop it.

chapters.title: What Cressida Saw
chapters.summary: On the stand, Cressida breaks: she saw Tobias strike his father and helped stage the drowning to protect the succession, believing Mara already lost to the sea. Her testimony damns her as much as Tobias. Tobias flees the courthouse. POV: Cressida, her only chapter. Emotional beat: ruin chosen over the rot of silence.

chapters.title: The Tide Gives It Up
chapters.summary: Tobias runs for his boat at Gannet Point as the spring tide turns. Mara confronts him at the water's edge — the witness everyone swore was dead, alive and naming him. Voss arrives to find the law's answer and Mara's hanging in the same balance. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: the climax, two justices on one shore.

chapters.title: The Confession That Counts
chapters.summary: Tobias, trapped by the tide and by Mara's testimony, confesses — and Voss chooses the law, taking him alive to the reopened inquest, because a stolen justice would let the estate's money rewrite even this. Halloran is arrested; Cressida's sentence is weighed against her testimony. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: the cost of doing it the slow, lawful way.

chapters.title: The Portrait Restored
chapters.summary: Evie restores the slashed canvas, painting Mara's face back where the family tried to cut it out. Mara, legally alive again, claims her inheritance and leaves Blackwater House to the sea. Voss files his report, keeps one letter, and watches the tide take the rest. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: quiet, earned resolution — memory as the only incorruptible archive.
